ml_logistic_regression.learningObjective: Simulate binary classification, sigmoid probability mapping P(y=1|x) = 1 / (1 + e^-z), and decision boundary separation.

tokens.value: # Linear combination (log-odds): z = w * x + b
# Sigmoid activation squashes z into (0, 1) probability
# Decision rule: Class 1 if p >= 0.50 else Class 0

executionSteps.explanationEnglish: Binary Classification Problem: 8 samples belonging to Class 0 (Red) or Class 1 (Cyan) along feature axis X.
executionSteps.explanationHinglish: Binary Classification problem: 8 samples Class 0 ya Class 1 me belong karte hain.
executionSteps.consoleOutput: > [INIT] 8 binary samples loaded. Target: Learn separation boundary.

executionSteps.explanationEnglish: Linear log-odds z = w*x + b with initial parameters (w=0.6, b=-2.2). Linear output can exceed [0, 1].
executionSteps.explanationHinglish: Linear score z = w*x + b calculate hua (w=0.6, b=-2.2). Linear output range 0 se 1 ke bahar ja sakti hai.
executionSteps.consoleOutput: > [LOG-ODDS] z = 0.60*x - 2.20. Mapping to non-linear probability required.

executionSteps.explanationEnglish: Sigmoid Transformation: P(y=1|x) = 1 / (1 + e^-z). Scores smoothly squashed into valid probabilities [0.0, 1.0].
executionSteps.explanationHinglish: Sigmoid S-curve: Har point ki probability 0.0 aur 1.0 ke beech squash ho gayi.
executionSteps.consoleOutput: > [SIGMOID] Formed S-curve. Threshold line P=0.50 applied.

executionSteps.explanationEnglish: Decision Boundary Condition: P = 0.50 occurs when z = 0 => w*x + b = 0 => x* = -b/w = 3.67.
executionSteps.explanationHinglish: Decision Boundary condition: P = 0.50 tab hota hai jab z = 0 => x* = -b/w = 3.67.
executionSteps.consoleOutput: > [BOUNDARY] Candidate separator at x = 3.58. 1 sample misclassified.

executionSteps.explanationEnglish: Gradient Optimization: Steepness w increases to 2.20, b adjusts to -7.90. Steep transition between classes.
executionSteps.explanationHinglish: Gradient descent se w = 2.20 aur b = -7.90 update hua. Sigmoid transition bohot sharp ho gaya.
executionSteps.consoleOutput: > [OPTIMIZATION] Log-loss reduced to 0.12. Accuracy reaches 100%.

executionSteps.explanationEnglish: Optimal Convergence: Boundary x* = 3.60 cleanly partitions Class 0 (x < 3.60) and Class 1 (x >= 3.60).
executionSteps.explanationHinglish: Final model converge ho gaya: Boundary x* = 3.60 par Class 0 aur Class 1 perfectly separated hain.
executionSteps.consoleOutput: > [CONVERGED] Optimal boundary x* = 3.60 | Minimized Binary Cross-Entropy Loss = 0.06

ml_knn_classification.learningObjective: Simulate instance-based majority voting, Euclidean distance metrics, and the effect of k parameter on decision confidence.

executionSteps.explanationEnglish: Unlabeled query point Q(4.2, 5.2) placed between Class A (Amber) and Class B (Cyan) clusters.
executionSteps.explanationHinglish: Query point Q(4.2, 5.2) feature space me aaya. Isko Class A ya Class B assign karna hai.
executionSteps.consoleOutput: > [INIT] Query Q(4.2, 5.2) placed. Computing Euclidean distances to all 10 points.

executionSteps.explanationEnglish: Compute Euclidean distance d = sqrt((x_q - x_i)^2 + (y_q - y_i)^2) from Q to all 10 training points.
executionSteps.explanationHinglish: Query point Q se sabhi 10 samples tak ka Euclidean distance calculate kiya gaya.
executionSteps.consoleOutput: > [DISTANCE] Closest points: Point #4 (dist=1.22), Point #5 (dist=1.77), Point #9 (dist=1.53)...

executionSteps.explanationEnglish: Evaluation at k = 1: Expanding circle reaches closest point #4 (Class A, dist=1.22). Prediction = Class A.
executionSteps.explanationHinglish: k = 1 par: Nearest neighbor point #4 (Class A) hai. Vote: 1 Class A vs 0 Class B. Sensitive to single point noise.
executionSteps.consoleOutput: > [k=1] Nearest: Point #4 (Class A). Vote: A=1, B=0 => Classified as Class A.

executionSteps.explanationEnglish: Evaluation at k = 3: Radius expands to 1.80. Encloses 3 neighbors (Point #4 [A], Point #9 [B], Point #5 [B]). Majority = Class B (2 vs 1).
executionSteps.explanationHinglish: k = 3 par: Radius 1.80 tak bada. 3 neighbors mile (1 Class A, 2 Class B). Majority vote Class B ke paas gaya.
executionSteps.consoleOutput: > [k=3] Neighbors: 2 Class B, 1 Class A. Majority vote => Classified as Class B.

executionSteps.explanationEnglish: Evaluation at k = 5: Radius expands to 2.15. Encloses 5 neighbors (2 Class A, 3 Class B). Majority stable = Class B (3 vs 2).
executionSteps.explanationHinglish: k = 5 par: Radius 2.15 hua. 5 neighbors me 3 Class B aur 2 Class A hain. Result Class B confirm hua.
executionSteps.consoleOutput: > [k=5] Neighbors: 3 Class B, 2 Class A. Robust majority => Classified as Class B.

executionSteps.explanationEnglish: Decision Boundary Summary: KNN classifies instances by local neighborhood density. Smooth boundary achieved at k=5.
executionSteps.explanationHinglish: KNN summary: Local neighborhood density ke base par point classify hua. k=5 par robust classification.
executionSteps.consoleOutput: > [FINAL] Prediction: Class B (Cyan) with 60% neighborhood confidence.

ml_decision_tree.learningObjective: Simulate recursive orthogonal axis-aligned splits, Gini Impurity reduction G = 1 - sum(p_i^2), and tree branching.

executionSteps.explanationEnglish: Root Node State: 10 samples (6 Class 0, 4 Class 1) mixed. Gini Impurity G = 1 - (0.6^2 + 0.4^2) = 0.48 (High impurity).
executionSteps.explanationHinglish: Root Node: 10 samples mixed hain (6 Class 0, 4 Class 1). Gini impurity 0.48 hai (Maximum mixing).
executionSteps.consoleOutput: > [ROOT] Total: 10 samples | 6 Class 0, 4 Class 1 | Gini Impurity = 0.48

executionSteps.explanationEnglish: Evaluate Candidate Splits: Testing vertical cuts (X1) and horizontal cuts (X2) to find maximum Information Gain.
executionSteps.explanationHinglish: Candidate splits evaluate ho rahe hain: Vertical aur horizontal cuts test kiye ja rahe hain.
executionSteps.consoleOutput: > [EVAL] Best Split found: Vertical cut at X1 = 4.0 (Information Gain = 0.28).

executionSteps.explanationEnglish: First Split (X1 <= 4.0): Vertical partition created. Left space (X1 <= 4.0) contains ONLY Class 0 (Pure Leaf, Gini=0.00).
executionSteps.explanationHinglish: Pehla Split (X1 <= 4.0): Vertical partition hua. Left region me sirf Class 0 hai (100% Pure, Gini=0.00).
executionSteps.consoleOutput: > [SPLIT 1] X1 <= 4.0: Left Child -> Pure Class 0 (4 samples) | Right Child -> Mixed (6 samples).

executionSteps.explanationEnglish: Second Split on Right Subregion: Horizontal cut at X2 <= 5.0 partitions the remaining mixed quadrant.
executionSteps.explanationHinglish: Second Split: Right subregion me horizontal cut X2 <= 5.0 lagaya gaya.

executionSteps.explanationEnglish: Pure Terminal Leaves: All 3 subregions have reached 100% purity (Gini Impurity = 0.00). Tree growth stops.
executionSteps.explanationHinglish: Teeno subregions 100% pure ho chuke hain (Gini = 0.00). Tree construction complete.

ml_activation_functions.learningObjective: Simulate and contrast Sigmoid, Tanh, ReLU, and Leaky ReLU activations alongside their first derivatives, illustrating how deep saturation causes vanishing gradients.

executionSteps.explanationEnglish: Sigmoid Activation & Saturation: Output f(z) = 1/(1+e^-z) bounded in [0, 1]. Maximum derivative f'(0) = 0.25. When |z| > 2, derivative drops to near zero (< 0.05).
executionSteps.explanationHinglish: Sigmoid Activation: Output 0 se 1 ke beech rehta hai. Maximum derivative sirf 0.25 hai. |z| > 2 hone par derivative lagbhag 0 ho jata hai (Saturation).
executionSteps.consoleOutput: > [SIGMOID] z = 2.20 -> f(z) = 0.900 | Gradient f'(z) = 0.090 (Severe Saturation)

executionSteps.explanationEnglish: Tanh Zero-Centered Activation: Output in [-1, +1]. Peak derivative f'(0) = 1.0 at origin. Better zero-centered gradient flow than Sigmoid, but still saturates at tails.
executionSteps.explanationHinglish: Tanh Activation: Output -1 se +1 me rehta hai. Center par derivative 1.0 hai, par bade values par ye bhi saturate hota hai.
executionSteps.consoleOutput: > [TANH] z = 2.20 -> f(z) = 0.975 | Gradient f'(z) = 0.049 | Zero-centered

executionSteps.explanationEnglish: ReLU Non-Saturating Activation: f(z) = max(0, z). For any positive input z > 0, gradient is ALWAYS exactly 1.0. Completely prevents vanishing gradients.
executionSteps.explanationHinglish: ReLU Activation: Positive input ke liye derivative humesha constant 1.0 rehta hai. Vanishing gradient problem permanently khatam!
